<objective>
Guide brownfield onboarding for an existing codebase by routing through the existing GSD primitives in the safe order: codebase map → docs ingest → project initialization → onboarding summary.
**Creates or confirms:**
- the codebase map from `/gsd-map-codebase` (served by `@gsd/codebase`, not installed here)
- the `project`, `requirement`, `milestone` and `phase` entities — project setup from `/gsd-new-project` or `/gsd-ingest-docs`
- the onboarding summary — a lightweight index of what was learned and the next command (shown, not written)
**Non-goals:** This command does not execute phases, ship work, or overwrite existing planning artifacts without an explicit gate.
</objective>

# /gsd-onboard Workflow
One-command onboarding for an existing or unknown repo. This workflow is a thin
renderer around a projection computed in Step 1 from the spec and the repository; the routing is its `next_action`.
`specforge gsd reference gsd-core/references/gsd-run-resolver.md`
## 1. Render the Onboarding Projection
Parse `--fast`:
- `--fast` passes `--fast` to `init onboard`. Fast mode accepts the fast map for lightweight onboarding only; `next_action` still decides whether complete map work is required before project setup.
- `--text` forces text-mode choices for runtimes without `conversational prompting`.
There is no `init onboard` projection here: compute it from the spec and the repository, from the git worktree root:
```bash
# One projection, computed here (--fast changes nothing: there is no fast map to accept):

ENTITIES=$(specforge export --kinds project,milestone,phase,requirement --format brief 2>/dev/null | jq -c '[.nodes[]|{id,kind}]')   # a project is not linked to its milestones, so the listing is by kind; [] when there is none
# Existing ADR/PRD/SPEC/RFC documents:

DOC_CANDIDATES=$(find . -type f \( -path '*/adr/*' -o -path '*/adrs/*' -o -path '*/prd/*' -o -path '*/prds/*' -o -path '*/rfc/*' -o -path '*/rfcs/*' -o -name 'ADR-*.md' -o -name 'PRD-*.md' -o -name 'SPEC-*.md' -o -name 'RFC-*.md' \) -not -path './.git/*' 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
ONBOARDING_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)
Work out these fields from `ENTITIES`, `DOC_CANDIDATES` and git (no projection supplies them):

- `next_action.kind`, `next_action.command`, `next_action.reason`, `next_action.missing`: the first of these that holds — `map-codebase` (a brownfield repo whose project planning is not complete; command `/gsd-map-codebase`, or `/gsd-map-codebase --fast` with `--fast`), `ingest-docs` (doc candidates and no project; `/gsd-ingest-docs`), `new-project` (no project; `/gsd-new-project`), `partial-planning` (some of the project, requirements and roadmap exist but not all; `missing` names the rest), else `write-summary`
- `handoff_commands.ingest_docs`, `handoff_commands.manager`, `handoff_commands.new_project`, `handoff_commands.onboard`: `/gsd-ingest-docs`, `/gsd-manager`, `/gsd-new-project`, `/gsd-onboard`
- `map_readiness`: `unavailable` (`@gsd/codebase`, which serves `/gsd-map-codebase`, is not installed here); `codebase_map_summary_status` and `codebase_map_final_status`: `not installed`

- `project_exists`: `ENTITIES` holds a `project` (the project is in the spec); `requirements_exists`, `roadmap_exists`: `requirement` entities, `milestone` and `phase` entities in `ENTITIES`; `planning_exists`: any of them; `state_exists`: the same as `project_exists` (the project state is computed, never a file)
- `is_brownfield`: the repository has files other than `*.spec` (`git ls-files`); `fast_mode`: `--fast` was parsed; `has_codebase_map`, `has_fast_codebase_map`: false
- `missing_codebase_map_files`, `missing_fast_codebase_map_files`: not applicable (no map is expected here)
- `has_docs_candidates`: `DOC_CANDIDATES` is above 0; `doc_candidate_count`: `DOC_CANDIDATES`; `onboarding_summary_exists`: false (the summary is shown, never written)
- `commit_docs`: false; `text_mode`: the `--text` flag; `has_git`, `git_worktree_root`, `in_nested_subdir`: from `git rev-parse` (nested when `--show-toplevel` is above the current directory)
- `response_language`

**If `response_language` is set:** All user-facing output of this workflow — narration between tool calls, status updates, progress notes, findings, questions, prompts, and explanations — MUST be presented in `{response_language}`. Technical terms, code, file paths, and subagent prompts stay in English — only user-facing output is translated.
Set:

- `TEXT_MODE=true` if `--text` is present or `text_mode` is true. When `TEXT_MODE` is active, replace every `conversational prompting` call below with a plain-text numbered list and ask the user to type their choice number — required for non-Claude runtimes (OpenAI Codex, Antigravity, etc.) where `conversational prompting` is not available.

## How to work
- **Computed is never written.** A status, a progress, a position and a count are computed from the graph. Where the
workflow says to update one, there is nothing to do.
- **Harness fields have one writer**: the command of `@gsd/core` that owns them (`specforge gsd <command>`; `specforge gsd help` lists them), never `specforge set`.
- **A command step's line has no arguments.** The step names the command; this text gives its arguments. Every
`--by` names who answers: `--by "<user>"` for a person, the agent's name for an agent.
- **Judges record their own verdicts** with `specforge gsd record-verdict` (the agent's body says how). An
orchestrator never records a verdict on a judge's behalf.
- **A refused call** (`gate_failed`, `human_only`, `stale_revision`, `invalid_input`) is reported to the user with its
message. Never edit the spec to get around it.
- **An agent that `@gsd/core` does not install** (`gsd-debugger`, `gsd-ui-researcher`, `gsd-ui-checker`,
`gsd-security-auditor`, `gsd-code-reviewer`, `gsd-codebase-mapper`, ...) is skipped, and the skip is said.
- **Spawning an agent** on this host: as the adapter header above says (the agent is the installed `gsd-<name>`). The model is the installed agent's own: skip any model resolution.
- **References** the workflow names are read with `specforge gsd reference <path>`.
- **Ids in the shell blocks.** `$PHASE_ID` and `$PLAN_ID` are the entity the run is about (the end of this text names
it), `$MILESTONE` is the current milestone and `$PROJECT` the project (the end of this text names them too).
